title: Can I BEAT 3D Glasses?
summary: The creator tries to earn chess.com's '3D Glasses' award for using the 3D piece set. He switches the in-game piece theme to the 3D Staunton pieces ('a crime against humanity'), plays a normal rapid game in the public pool as Black vs a 2000-rated player, plays 1.e4 e5 for once (aiming for a Stafford Gambit, declined), and wins by resignation after Bc5 wins the queen (brilliant move). The award doesn't unlock; he then switches the whole interface to the 3D board, starts a game vs the Martin bot and resigns, and still doesn't get it.
rules: Cosmetic requirement: play using the 3D piece set / 3D board theme.
win_condition: Win the game (and earn the 3D Glasses award - not obtained in the video).

board.shape_notes: standard; later a true 3D perspective board
board.theme_notes: 3D Staunton piece set (rendered 3D pieces on flat green chess.com board), then full 3D board theme. Thumbnail in sheet s5.

current_impl_issues: Implemented as 'fogx' half-fog (only see enemies on dark squares) - invented. Video is normal chess with a 3D piece theme; mode should be a cosmetic 3D-pieces skin over standard chess vs a ~2000 opponent, player Black.
evidence: Transcript 0:01 '3D glasses award for using the 3D pieces... win one game'; 0:32 '3D Staunton pieces'; public rapid pool, black pieces; 1:03 E5/Stafford; 8:11 resignation; 8:45 no award; 9:13 3D board, Martin; 9:50 'it has not worked'.
